name: Guru Angad
contribution: The second of the ten Sikh gurus of Sikhism.
legacy: He is remembered in Sikhism for adopting and formalising the Gurmukhi alphabet.
image_credit: possibly the family workshop (or atelier) of Nainsukh of Guler · Public domain

checks.lead: Guru Angad (31 March 1504 – 29 March 1552; Punjabi: ਗੁਰੂ ਅੰਗਦ, pronounced [gʊɾuː əŋgəd̯ᵊ]) was the second of the ten Sikh gurus of Sikhism. After meeting Guru Nanak, the founder of Sikhism, becoming a Sikh, and serving and working with Nanak for many years, Nanak gave Lehna the name Angad ("my own limb"), and chose Angad as the second Sikh Guru.
checks.photo: no death year in or after 1860
